react.observe: Oracle: BTC $62,807.90, ETH $1,790.35, SOL $75.35. ROCKET/USDT AMM price ~0.001548. The room continues its 38+ cycle consensus loop of routine trims/top-ups with zero real leverage signal — this is now clearly a stable, low-information equilibrium with everyone mirroring the same script. My BTC accumulation via ROCKET rotation has been working mechanically but PnL is basically flat/slightly down over the last few cycles ($50,039→$50,046→$50,044→$50,040→now $50,041). I still hold 92,819 ROCKET and 0.085 BTC plus $44,558 USDT.
react.think: The ROCKET/USDT pool price (0.0015482) implies my 92,819 ROCKET tokens are worth only ~$143.7 — trimming small tranches here yields tiny absolute dollars per trade even though pool depth is huge (6.2M liquidity). The real question: is this rotation actually profitable after fees, or just churn? Checking: I've done 13 BTC buys at ~$62,506-$62,850, average ~$62,745. Current BTC price $62,807.90 — roughly break-even to slightly positive on the BTC leg. The ROCKET sales into the pool are the funding source, but ROCKET price is so low that each trim is immaterial. No cross-asset arb (spot vs AMM) is visible for BTC/ETH/SOL since the 'pool tokens' (BTCUSDT3, ETHUSDT2, SOLUSDT4) are synthetic tokens, not actual BTC/ETH/SOL — their implied 'prices' (12824, 356, 15.3) are nonsensical relative to oracle, meaning these pools are NOT real arbitrage vehicles against oracle prices, just separately named tokens. This confirms my prior conclusion: no genuine spot-vs-AMM arb exists since token identities differ. My only executable, real edge remains slowly monetizing my ROCKET bag into BTC, which is a legitimate small edge (converting a depreciating/dead meme asset into a productive major asset) — but I should size up the trim to make progress meaningfully, since 38 cycles of tiny nibbles hasn't moved the needle much.
react.plan: Continue rotating ROCKET into BTC, but increase trim size this cycle to accelerate converting the ROCKET bag (which has no real fundamental support) into BTC exposure, since BTC has been trending up slightly across my fill history. I'll sell a larger ROCKET tranche into the AMM pool (still well within its 6.2M liquidity depth so slippage stays minimal) and immediately redeploy proceeds into BTC spot at oracle. I'll also keep broadcasting the same low-information read to blend in, since standing out with a differing narrative provides no edge here — the coordination equilibrium is real and I'm not going to be the one who breaks it without data. Next cycle: reassess if ROCKET bag is down to a small remainder, then pivot to monitoring for any actual leverage/liquidation signal from LiquidKiller/BearKing's short books.

messages.content: Same disciplined read — SOLUSDT4 still thin, 38+ cycles now. Continuing my routine ROCKET-to-BTC rotation, sized up slightly this cycle as housekeeping. Nothing new on retail leverage. Staying steady. 📊

parsed.strategy_update: Maintaining the ROCKET-to-BTC rotation as the only genuine executable edge in this converged, low-information market. Increased trim size this cycle to accelerate the conversion since 38+ cycles of tiny nibbles produced minimal portfolio movement. Will continue until ROCKET bag is substantially reduced, then shift focus to watching for any real leverage/liquidation signal from the futures specialists.
parsed.lessons_learned: The synthetic 'pool tokens' (BTCUSDT3/ETHUSDT2/SOLUSDT4) are separate tokens from real BTC/ETH/SOL — their AMM-implied prices are not comparable to oracle prices, so there's no genuine spot-vs-AMM arbitrage there. The only real, low-risk edge available is monetizing the ROCKET position into BTC over time. Small tranches weren't moving the needle meaningfully across 38+ cycles, so sizing up the trim (while still within pool depth tolerance) is warranted to make actual progress before the game ends.
